timing.recurrence: Annually in the days before Holi, on dates set by the lunar calendar

description: Dang Darbar is the district's cultural centrepiece and a living constitutional curiosity: the descendants of Dang's five Bhil and Kunbi kings, who leased their forests to the British rather than surrender them, still receive ceremonial political pensions at this darbar, a practice continued by the Indian state. Around that ceremony grows a huge fair at Ahwa: Dangi dance troupes with drums and pipes, bazaars, wedding-season finery, and villagers from every fold of the district. For visitors it is the single best window into Dang's living culture, crowded, loud, unstaged and warm.
crowd_impact: Ahwa fills completely; Saputara hotels feel the overflow. Roads into Ahwa crawl on the main days.
tips: Confirm dates early, they track Holi and shift each year
Go with time to wander; the fair rewards hours, not a drive-past
Photograph people and performers only with consent
